newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bonds turn cautious, data to come.
newsitem.headline: Australia bonds turn cautious, data to come.

text.p: *Australian bonds ended little changed from Monday's closing levels as domestic institutions took a more cautionary stance in view of the market's recent gyrations.
*Aggressively bid T-bond tender fails to lift the market.

Australian bonds ended little changed from Monday's closing levels as domestic institutions took a more cautionary stance in view of the market's recent gyrations and ahead of some key data later this week.
"The feeling is the next big move is going to come from offshore, so I suspect we're just going to sit tight for a couple of days before the U.S. PPI," one trader said.
That data for November is due on Wednesday, and is followed by the U.S. CPI for the same month on Thursday.
Sandwiched in between will be the local November labour force report, one of the last major reports of the year.
An aggressively bid A$600 million Treasury bond tender failed to lift the market, being offset by a retracement in U.S. Treasuries in Tokyo after firming in New York.
The A$400 million of the relatively new September 2009 bonds fetched a weighted average yield of 7.455 percent and in the middle of a tight one basis point bid range.
The stock was seen quoted at around 7.475/7.435 percent when final bids went in at 12.45 a.m. (0145 GMT).
The A$200 million of April 2000 bonds were taken out by one investor at 6.690 percent, having been quoted at 6.735/6.695 percent at final bidding time.
AUD VS 3-YR 10-YR * AUD 3-YR/10-YR SPREAD

Yield spreads reversed an initial spread tightening against the U.S. reflecting the subdued local activity. Canadian debt continued to outpace the bloc, rebounding from last week's heavy sell-off, while N.Z. bonds turned jittery as there was still no word on the make-up of the country's new government.

The 10-year bond contract continues to meet solid resistance around 92.670, and a further rejection today contributed to the softening trend going into the close. Initial support is seen at 92.615.
